newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AssiDoman stops Russian plant operation.
newsitem.headline: AssiDoman stops Russian plant operation.

text.p: Swedish forestry company AssiDoman AB said on Thursday that it had been forced to stop operations at its Segezhabumprom pulp and paper mill in Russia.

Stratton Paper Company, which has managed the plant since January, could take no further initiatives until tax issues, postponed payment of pension funds, heating payments and cutting rights issues were settled, AssiDoman said.
"The future of Segezhabumprom pulp and paper mill in Karelia has become uncertain," AssiDoman said in a statement.
"The unsolved situation is paralysing the company's possibilites to act long term," it said.

Despite having no formal financial responsibility, Stratton Paper Company has loaned Segezha some $10 million for salaries, fuel oil payments and other necessary expenditures to keep the mill going. AssiDoman owns half of Stratton Paper Company.

AssiDoman said the owners had been closely negotiating with IFC and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development about a three year investment programme totalling about $100 million. It said these talks were continuing.
